description:
Xin chào mọi người! Mình yêu thích khoa học vũ trụ, thiên văn học và công nghệ. Mình tham gia NASA Space Apps Challenge với mong muốn học hỏi, sáng tạo và cùng giải quyết những vấn đề liên quan đến không gian.

Mình đang tìm kiếm những thành viên nhiệt tình, có tinh thần trách nhiệm và yêu thích khám phá. Các kỹ năng về lập trình, nghiên cứu, thiết kế và phân tích dữ liệu sẽ là lợi thế. Hãy cùng nhau học hỏi và tạo nên những ý tưởng đột phá!
summary:
COSMOS QUEST is a web-based 3D space engineering simulation and educational game where players take on the role of a mission architect to design and launch spacecraft.

What we developed: Built an intuitive interactive interface featuring realistic 3D planetary globes (the Moon, Earth, and Mars) using the Three.js library, integrated real-world scientific data systems from NASA (such as NASA Earthdata Search and NASA Worldview), and included an automated Vietnamese text-to-speech feature for mission result reports.

Challenge addressed: Transformed dry astronomy and aerospace concepts into a dynamic experience, helping players solve complex resource-balancing problems involving budget ( ≤ $100M), payload mass, power, and scientific value.

Why it matters: The project serves as a powerful tool to support STEM/STEAM education, spark a passion for space exploration among students, and develop practical systems-design thinking.
details:
1. What does this project do, and how does it work?

  • General Description: COSMOS QUEST is an educational space simulation game (EdTech Space Simulation Game) that combines real-world science with an intuitive, interactive experience.
  • How It Works: Players can explore dynamic 3D planetary models (Earth, the Moon, and Mars), plan space exploration missions, interact directly with the control interface, and experience simulated audio along with speech synthesis features that guide them through key mission milestones. The system runs entirely on a web platform, allowing players to easily access it from any device without complex installations.

2. What benefits does the project bring?

  • Visual Education: Transforms dry scientific data from NASA into a vivid simulation experience, helping students and space enthusiasts easily absorb knowledge of astronomy and space physics.
  • Sparking STEM Passion: Encourages logical thinking, scientific curiosity, and a desire to explore outer space among the younger generation through a "learning through play" approach.
  • Easy Public Access: Thanks to public deployment on a web platform, anyone can experience it directly via a single link without needing an account or special permissions.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

  • Spreading Open Science Data: Raises community awareness about the importance of applying real-world data from aerospace agencies to daily life and general education.
  • Teaching Support Tool: Can be directly applied in Science, Physics, or Computer Science classes at schools to visually illustrate the solar system and orbital mechanics.

4. What tools, programming languages, and software were used?

  • Programming Languages: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript (Front-end web development).
  • 3D Libraries & Technologies: Three.js to build and render interactive 3D space models.
  • Interface & Utilities: Web Speech API (speech synthesis) and real-time simulated sound effects.
  • Scientific Data Sources: Leveraged and integrated data from open scientific research systems (such as NASA Earthdata Search and NASA Worldview).
  • Development & Deployment Platforms: Visual Studio Code on Windows, Git/GitHub for source code management, and GitHub Pages for public web deployment.

5. Creativity of the project

  • Combining Real-World Data with Gamification: Instead of merely viewing static images or reading plain documents, the project allows users to hands-on interact with, operate, and experience space from the perspective of a real aerospace engineer.
  • Multi-Sensory Experience: Integrates real-time 3D space graphics with an audio system and smart voice effects, creating a strong sense of immersion for players.

6. Factors considered by the team

  • Scientific Accuracy: Ensuring models and simulation information are based on reliable, real-world data provided by leading organizations like NASA.
  • Usability and User Experience (UX/UI): Designing an intuitive, smooth interface and optimizing 3D graphics performance in web browsers so users do not experience lag or stuttering.
  • Global Accessibility: Publishing the project online completely free of charge, ensuring that anyone (from the judging panel to the general public) can access and enjoy a seamless experience immediately.
